name: Middle Blue Green
lede: Middle Blue Green is a pale, soft [[blue-green]], picked up by Wikipedia's extended color lists and matched, in our data, to a crowd of near-identical ISCC-NBS 1955 names.

sections.title: One hue, many filed names
sections.body:
The name follows ordinary modifier grammar, "middle" plus the parent hue [[blue-green]], and comes to our library from Wikipedia's lists, with no further paper trail [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists filed at least seventeen separate commercial and descriptive names into the same color block as this shade, among them AprilSky, Aqua Queen, Brook Green, Electra and Robin Egg [1]. That crowding is itself the point: dozens of paint and textile brands each wanted their own name for roughly this one pale aqua [1].

Its nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[nile-blue]], darker and duller, with [[light-sulphate-green]] and [[turquoise]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in only 5 of 23,781 paintings, 0.02 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 4 [2]. That makes it rarer than 77 percent of the named colors we track [2]. The earliest dated painting with it is from 1847, by A. Hashagen, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2].

questions.q: Why does our data file so many other names into the same ISCC-NBS 1955 block as Middle Blue Green?
choices: Many brands each coined their own name for roughly the same pale aqua
The color changes name depending on the season
It is the only pale aqua the ISCC-NBS recognized
A printing error duplicated one entry seventeen times
questions.answer: Many brands each coined their own name for roughly the same pale aqua

questions.q: True or false: Middle Blue Green is common in our painting archive.
